words.en: O crowned one, wearer of the diadem
words.g: f. voc. sg. of किरीटिनी (feminine of किरीटिन् ‘having a diadem’, possessive taddhita -इन् on किरीट)

words.en: O you of the great thunderbolt
O you who blaze with a thousand eyes

words.g: indeclinable (conjunctive particle); adds the last epithet and the name ऐन्द्रि to the series
f. voc. sg. of ऐन्द्री (taddhita अण् on इन्द्र ‘belonging to Indra’, feminine in -ī)
f. voc. sg. of नारायणी (ī-stem, feminine of नारायण)
n. nom. sg. of नमस् (s-stem); subject of अस्तु
second-person pronoun युष्मद्, enclitic dat. sg.; dative with नमः

sandhi.note: a + ai → ai: the vowel of the particle disappears into the ai. Read च ऐन्द्रि, not a form of इन्द्र.
-aḥ before a: the visarga (as ru) becomes u, a + u gives o, and the initial a of अस्तु is absorbed into the o (avagraha). The same junction closes every stanza of the refrain (11.8–23).

samasa.sense: Aindrī with Indra’s vajra in hand (8.21 वज्रहस्ता)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a dvigu (सहस्रनयन: a numeral compound standing before a further member)
samasa.alt: Also a bahuvrīhi, सहस्रं नयनानि उज्ज्वलानि यस्याः सा ‘whose thousand eyes blaze’. The sense is the same; the tatpuruṣa keeps उज्ज्वला as the word that describes her.

samasa.vigraha: वृत्रस्य प्राणाः वृत्रप्राणाः; वृत्रप्राणान् हरति इति वृत्रप्राणहरा
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (हर = √हृ with the agent affix a after its object) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (वृत्रप्राण)
samasa.literal: she who takes away the life-breaths of Vṛtra
samasa.sense: slayer of Vṛtra — Indra’s great deed, ascribed to his power

morph.note: किरीट ‘diadem’ + the possessive -इन् gives किरीटिन् ‘crowned’; the feminine adds -ī (किरीटिनी), and the vocative shortens it: किरीटिनि.

Taddhita: इन्द्र + अ (अण्) with vṛddhi of the first vowel (इ → ऐ) gives ऐन्द्र ‘of Indra’; feminine ऐन्द्री, vocative ऐन्द्रि. वैष्णवी, माहेश्वरी and कौमारी in the stanzas before are formed the same way.
Imperative third singular of √अस्: with नमः ‘let there be homage’; the dative ते names the one honoured.

mantras.anvaya: हे किरीटिनि महावज्रे सहस्रनयनोज्ज्वले वृत्रप्राणहरे च ऐन्द्रि नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: A chain of vocatives ending in the name ऐन्द्रि; च adds the last epithet. The refrain नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते is the main clause.
mantras.lit: O crowned one, O you of the great thunderbolt, O you who blaze with a thousand eyes, and O Aindrī, taker of Vṛtra’s life — O Nārāyaṇī, let homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Crowned, wielding the great thunderbolt, ablaze with a thousand eyes, Aindrī who took the life of Vṛtra — Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.

comm.t: The seventh of the Mātṛkā stanzas (11.13–21). The Goddess is praised as Aindrī, Indra’s power, as she came to the battlefield in 8.21 (वज्रहस्ता … गजराजोपरि स्थिता … सहस्रनयना यथा शक्रः) and struck Raktabīja with her thunderbolt (8.42, 8.46). Every attribute is Indra’s: the diadem, the vajra, the thousand eyes, the killing of Vṛtra.

In 8.13–14 the powers of the gods leave their bodies with the same form, ornaments and mounts as the gods themselves. The hymn names each Mātṛkā by her god’s deed: Vārāhī lifts the earth on her tusk (11.17), Nārasiṃhī strikes the daityas (11.18), Aindrī slays Vṛtra. The Vedic victory of Indra is credited to the power through which he won it.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the name वज्रिणी (name 944), ‘she who holds the thunderbolt’. The image is shared; the two texts are separate works.

words.g: n. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrumental of manner, ‘in the form of’

words.en: O you by whom the great army of the daityas was slain
O you of the mighty roar

words.g: n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (the first member names the form)
samasa.literal: by the own-form that is Śivadūtī
samasa.sense: as Śivadūtī, the form that sent Śiva as messenger (8.24–28)
the name given in 8.28: यतो नियुक्तो दौत्येन तया देव्या शिवः स्वयम्

samasa.vigraha: महत् बलं महाबलम्; दैत्यानां महाबलं दैत्यमहाबलम्; हतं दैत्यमहाबलं यया सा
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (दैत्यमहाबल) and a karmadhāraya (महाबल); महत् takes the form महा- before the noun it qualifies
samasa.literal: she by whom the great army of the daityas was slain
samasa.alt: बल can also mean ‘strength’: हताः दैत्याः यया सा च महाबला च, ‘slayer of the daityas, of great might’. The compound is printed as one word, and बल ‘army’ with हत ‘slain’ reads more naturally; both senses fit the narrative.

samasa.sense: the howl of a hundred jackals (8.23 शिवाशतनिनादिनी) and her laughter (9.23)

morph.note: Instrumental of manner among vocatives, as माहेश्वरीस्वरूपेण in 11.14: ‘(you who appear) in the form of Śivadūtī’.
हत is the past participle (kta) of √हन् (adādi 2P ‘to strike, kill’); as the first member of a bahuvrīhi it gives the passive sense ‘by whom … was slain’.

mantras.anvaya: हे शिवदूतीस्वरूपेण (स्थिते) हतदैत्यमहाबले घोररूपे महारावे नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: The instrumental phrase describes the manner of her appearance; three bahuvrīhi vocatives follow; then the refrain.
mantras.lit: (You who are) in the form of Śivadūtī, O you by whom the great army of the daityas was slain, O you of terrible form, O you of the mighty roar — O Nārāyaṇī, let homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Appearing as Śivadūtī, destroyer of the daityas’ mighty host, terrible of form, loud of roar — Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Appearing’ supplies the participle implied by the instrumental of form.

comm.t: The eighth Mātṛkā stanza praises Śivadūtī, the fierce power that sprang from Caṇḍikā’s own body, howling like a hundred jackals (8.23). She sent Śiva as her envoy to Śumbha and Niśumbha (8.24–27) and so was named Śivadūtī, ‘she who has Śiva as messenger’ (8.28). Her laughter terrified the asuras (8.38, 9.23) and she devoured them (9.37, 9.41).

Unlike the six Mātṛkās before her, Śivadūtī is no god’s power but the Devī’s own: she comes from Caṇḍikā’s body, not from a god’s. The stanza thus moves from the gods’ śaktis back to the Goddess herself, completed by Cāmuṇḍā in 11.21.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the name शिवदूती (name 405). The name and its sense are shared Śākta usage; the two texts are separate works.

words.en: O you whose face is dreadful with tusks
O you adorned with a garland of heads

words.g: f. voc. sg. of चामुण्डा (proper name)
n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु

sandhi.note: The final s of the stem शिरस् becomes ru, then u before the voiced m, and a + u gives o: शिरोमाला.

samasa.vigraha: दंष्ट्राभिः करालम् दंष्ट्राकरालम्; दंष्ट्राकरालं वदनं यस्याः सा
samasa.literal: she whose face is frightful with tusks
samasa.sense: Kālī’s dreadful, gaping mouth (7.6 करालवदना, 7.8 अतिविस्तारवदना)

samasa.vigraha: शिरसां माला शिरोमाला; शिरोमाला विभूषणं यस्याः सा
samasa.literal: she whose ornament is a garland of heads
samasa.sense: wearing a garland of heads, as Kālī appears in 7.7 (नरमालाविभूषणा)

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (मथन = √मथ् with the agent affix -अन)
samasa.alt: Also a bahuvrīhi: मुण्डस्य मथनं यया सा, ‘she by whom the crushing of Muṇḍa (was done)’; or with मुण्ड in its common-noun sense ‘shaven head’, ‘crusher of heads’. The proper name fits the pairing with चामुण्डे.

morph.note: Vocative of चामुण्डा. The text gives the name’s origin in 7.27: because Kālī brought the heads of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, she would be known as Cāmuṇḍā (यस्माच्चण्डं च मुण्डं च … चामुण्डेति ततो लोके ख्याता देवि भविष्यसि). It is a name, not a regular compound.
मथन is an agent noun from √मथ् / मन्थ् (‘to churn, crush’) in -अन; feminine मथना, vocative मथने.

mantras.anvaya: हे दंष्ट्राकरालवदने शिरोमालाविभूषणे मुण्डमथने चामुण्डे नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two bahuvrīhi vocatives describing her appearance, the name with its explanatory epithet, then the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you whose face is dreadful with tusks, O you whose ornament is a garland of heads, O Cāmuṇḍā, O crusher of Muṇḍa — O Nārāyaṇī, let homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Fanged and fearful of face, garlanded with heads, Cāmuṇḍā, slayer of Muṇḍa — Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.

comm.t: The last Mātṛkā stanza praises Cāmuṇḍā, the Kālī who sprang from Ambikā’s brow (7.5–7), killed Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa (7.20–21) and received her name for it (7.27). In the Raktabīja battle she drank the demon’s blood so that no new asura could rise from it (8.53–61). The epithets are those of her first appearance: a gaping fanged mouth and a garland of heads.

With Cāmuṇḍā the series of nine forms (Brahmāṇī to Cāmuṇḍā, 11.13–21) is complete. In the Śākta tradition these forms are worshipped as the Mātṛkās, the ‘Mothers’, with Cāmuṇḍā often counted among them; the hymn presents them all as forms of one Nārāyaṇī.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names her चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी (name 756), ‘destroyer of the asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa’ — the same story in a different text.

words.g: f. voc. sg. of लक्ष्मी (ī-stem; nom. लक्ष्मीः)
f. voc. sg. of महाविद्या; compound (see Samāsa)
f. voc. sg. of पुष्टि (i-stem); the regular vocative is पुष्टे — here the stem form, as भूति in 11.23 (see flags)

words.en: O Svadhā, the offering to the ancestors

words.g: f. voc. sg. of ध्रुवा (feminine of the adjective ध्रुव ‘fixed, constant’)
f. voc. sg. of महारात्री (ī-stem by-form of रात्रि); compound (see Samāsa)
f. voc. sg. of महाविद्या read as महा + अविद्या; compound (see Samāsa)
n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु

sandhi.note: ā + a → ā. The Gita Press writes an avagraha to show that an a has merged into the ā: mahā + avidyā, not mahāvidyā. The sound is the same either way (see the variant).
The two vocatives are printed without a space; nothing changes at the junction.

samasa.sense: the supreme knowledge that frees (cf. 1.57 सा विद्या परमा मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता)
the night of dissolution, as in Brahmā’s hymn (1.79 कालरात्रिर्महारात्रिर्मोहरात्रिश्च दारुणा)

samasa.vigraha: महती अविद्या (महाविद्या), तत्सम्बुद्धौ; अविद्या = न विद्या
samasa.sense: the ignorance that binds, also her power (cf. 1.58 संसारबन्धहेतुश्च सैव)
samasa.alt: Without the avagraha (GRETIL, Freund) the word is महाविद्ये again, ‘great knowledge’, repeating the first line. The Gita Press reading pairs it with महारात्रि and balances महाविद्ये in the first line.

morph.note: लक्ष्मी is an ī-stem of the type that keeps visarga in the nominative (लक्ष्मीः); the vocative shortens the ī: लक्ष्मि. Contrast the ā-stems of the line, whose vocative ends in -e (लज्जे, श्रद्धे, स्वधे).

The i-stem vocative should be पुष्टे (guṇa of the final). The printed पुष्टि (written together with स्वधे) keeps the stem form, as भूति does in 11.23; Purāṇic verse allows such vocatives. The metre is unaffected.
रात्रि has a by-form रात्री (ī-stem); the vocative of महारात्री is महारात्रि. (Of the i-stem, used in 1.79, it would be महारात्रे.)

mantras.anvaya: हे लक्ष्मि लज्जे महाविद्ये श्रद्धे पुष्टि स्वधे ध्रुवे महारात्रि महाऽविद्ये नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Nine names in the vocative, each a power the Goddess is; then the refrain.
mantras.lit: O Lakṣmī, O Modesty, O Great Knowledge, O Faith, O Nourishment, O Svadhā, O Steadfast One, O Great Night, O Great Nescience — O Nārāyaṇī, let homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Fortune, Modesty, Great Knowledge, Faith, Nourishment, Svadhā, the Steadfast; Great Night and Great Ignorance — Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.

comm.t: After the nine warrior forms the hymn turns to abstract powers. Most of these names were already given her by Brahmā (1.73 स्वधा, 1.77 महाविद्या, 1.79 महारात्रिः, 1.80 लज्जा पुष्टिः) and by the gods (4.5 श्रीः … श्रद्धा … लज्जा; 5.44–58 लज्जा, श्रद्धा, लक्ष्मी).

The line ends on a pair of opposites: महाविद्या ‘great knowledge’ at the start of the first line, महाऽविद्या ‘great nescience’ at the end of the second. The Gita Press marks the second with an avagraha; other witnesses (GRETIL, Freund) read महाविद्ये twice. Both readings are traditional (corrections.json, variant).

The Gita Press reading states a teaching the text gives from the start: the same Mahāmāyā is the knowledge that liberates and the power that binds (1.57–58 सा विद्या परमा मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता … संसारबन्धहेतुश्च सैव). Knowledge and ignorance are not two goddesses.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has महाविद्या (name 584) and विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी (name 402), ‘whose form is both knowledge and ignorance’, and also लज्जा (740), पुष्टिः (444) and स्वधा (536). The pairing of knowledge and nescience is a shared Śākta idea; the texts are separate works.

flags.uncertain: Variant (recorded): महाऽविद्ये (Gita Press, kept) against महाविद्ये (GRETIL, Freund) — two readings, ‘great nescience’ or ‘great knowledge’; both traditional. The digital text prints पुष्टिस्वधे as one word; it is taken here as two vocatives (पुष्टि, a stem-form vocative for पुष्टे, and स्वधे), since a dvandva of two names would not stand in the vocative singular. If the joining is deliberate, the alternative is an irregular compound vocative of ‘Puṣṭi-Svadhā’.

words.g: f. voc. sg. of वरा (feminine of the adjective वर ‘best, choice’)
f. voc. sg. of भूति (i-stem); the regular vocative is भूते — here the stem form (see Morph)
f. voc. sg. of बाभ्रवी (taddhita on बभ्रु ‘tawny’, feminine in -ī)

words.en: O Tāmasī, you of the nature of tamas
words.g: f. voc. sg. of तामसी (taddhita अण् on तमस्, feminine in -ī)
f. voc. sg. of नियति (i-stem, regular vocative); see Morph for the alternative
second-person pronoun युष्मद्, nom. sg.; subject of प्रसीद
प्र + √सद् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to sit, settle’; present stem सीद-), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
f. voc. sg. of ईशा (feminine of ईश ‘ruler’)
n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु

sandhi.note: a + ī → e. The imperative and the vocative are written as one.
Final m before the consonant p becomes anusvāra.

morph.note: The i-stem vocative would be भूते. The text has भूति, a stem-form vocative found in Purāṇic verse (compare पुष्टि in 11.22). The syllable count is the same either way.

Taken as the regular vocative of नियति (नि + √यम्, kṛt -ति) ‘restraint, fixed order, destiny’, which fits a list of powers (मेधा, भूति). It can also be the vocative of नियता (kta of नि + √यम्) ‘self-restrained one’; the form is the same.
Imperative of प्र + √सद्: the root takes the present stem सीद- (सद् → सीद), and with प्र means ‘be pleased, be gracious’.
Taddhita: तमस् + अ with vṛddhi (त → ता) gives तामस ‘belonging to tamas’; feminine तामसी, vocative तामसि.

mantras.anvaya: हे मेधे सरस्वति वरे भूति बाभ्रवि तामसि नियते ईशे, त्वं प्रसीद। (हे) नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Seven vocatives, a prayer (त्वं प्रसीद) with an eighth vocative (ईशे) set inside it, then the refrain.
mantras.lit: O Medhā, O Sarasvatī, O excellent one, O Prosperity, O Bābhravī, O Tāmasī, O Niyati — you, be gracious, O sovereign Lady; O Nārāyaṇī, let homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Intelligence, Sarasvatī, most excellent, Prosperity, tawny Bābhravī, dark Tāmasī, Ordaining Power — be gracious, sovereign Lady. Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: बाभ्रवि and तामसि are rendered with their literal sense (‘tawny’, ‘dark’) as well as the name.

comm.t: The list of powers continues: intellect and speech (मेधा, सरस्वती), prosperity (भूति), and two names of her darker nature (बाभ्रवी, तामसी), closing with Niyati, the power that fixes the order of things. In the middle of the list the gods break into a direct prayer: त्वं प्रसीद, ‘be gracious’.

Medhā and Sarasvatī recall the gods’ hymn of chapter 4 (4.11 मेधासि देवि विदिताखिलशास्त्रसारा). Tāmasī is the Goddess as tamas, the power of sleep and dissolution: Brahmā’s hymn calls her the bearer of the three guṇas (1.78 गुणत्रयविभाविनी), and in the first carita she is Viṣṇu’s yoganidrā, his sleep (1.66, 1.69–71).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has मेधा (name 538) and सरस्वती (name 704). Shared names; separate works.

flags.uncertain: भूति (and पुष्टि in 11.22) are stem-form vocatives, not the regular भूते; kept as printed. नियते may be read as Niyati ‘destiny’ (chosen) or नियता ‘the self-restrained’. बाभ्रवी: lexically ‘tawny’ (from बभ्रु) or ‘belonging to Babhru’; the specific mythological reference is not stated in the text.
